stream_rule: Each stream is one polyline made of segments; a particle at phase ph is at tau = (ph + t) mod duration_s along it, moving at each segment speed_mps (display speed: the real duct air is ~20-23 m/s). count = density_per_m * length_m; phases evenly spread over duration_s with +-35% jitter; each particle has a fixed offset in a disc of radius jitter * duct_radius_m around the path. Streak tails are streak_s long. fade=true: size scales with sin(pi*tau/duration).

cutaway_rule: The model is pre-split: each part = the kept shell + a *_cut piece + an interior *_liner. A cutaway = hide the *_cut nodes (exactly what the video does; liners are always visible but only seen once the cut piece is hidden). The wedge clip planes are an alternative for section caps or an animated opening: three.js clippingPlanes with clipIntersection=true on clones of the materials of the *_cut and kept nodes.

translucent.rule: The video makes whole MATERIALS translucent (alpha 0.40; 0.35 in shot 2), so e.g. Steel on the cyclone goes see-through with the ducts. To match the video set opacity on those materials; to keep it to ducts only, clone the materials on duct_nodes. Use depthWrite=false and render the flow particles after the opaque pass.

notes: Cut 3 geometry (explainer.blend saved 12:01). Cut 4 was rendering when this was exported; re-run tools/ when cut 4 lands.

Edgebander 1 pickups: the 5 in drop (x 18.36, nearest the infeed) is taken as the head pickup (sawdust) and the 6 in drop (x 19.95) as the last pickup (PVC chips). Swap machines[EB1].pickups if that is wrong.
Streams marked in_video=false (CNC 2, EB 1 head chips, EB 2, panel saw) are built the same way from the kit centerlines; EB 2 and the panel saw start at the bottom of their drops.
Transfer blower speed is assumed (3,450 rpm); the manuals do not give it.
Flamex: no shutdowns are shown (interlocks not confirmed).
